gotchas: THE VENDOR CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE TRANSPORT. The B-LFP-48-150GC datasheet lists 'CAN-Bus Communication' under Safety & Intelligence. The Golf Cart User Manual, covering that same model by name, lists as a feature 'Pre-warning when battery is almost empty (communication by means of RS485)'. Two BSLBATT documents, one

B-LFP48-104GC IS NOT A BSLBATT MODEL as far as any document found goes. The 48 V golf-cart line is 52 / 72 / 105 / 135 / 150 / 205 Ah. '104' is most likely a retailer transcription of 105GC — but 'most likely' is how a bench day gets lost, so it is written down as unmatched rather than corrected.

The connector is not RJ45. The manual's port table gives 'Comm — GX16-4 — Charging communication interface' and 'Screen — GX16-6 — Display screen interface'. GX16 is a 16 mm circular aviation connector. Note also that the comm port is described as the CHARGING communication interface — it may exist to talk to the match

The display is a Samkoom touch panel on a separate '(J6)' port running a vendor BMS screen. It shows total voltage, current, capacity, per-cell max/min voltage with cell index, Tmax and an ISO insulation reading. That is a proprietary HMI link, not a documented protocol.
No baud rate, no address, no protocol name, no register. Nothing here is buildable. If somebody wants these, the route is a bench capture on the GX16-4 pins, not more reading.
unmappedReports: Insulation resistance (ISO). The datasheet specifies '≥20 MΩ/1000 VDC' and the BMS screen displays a live ISO value. No MetricKind, and on a traction pack it is the safety-relevant number., Per-cell voltage with cell index (Vmax/Vmin and 'No: M: B:' on the screen) — same gap as the PACE dialect., Passive balancing current, specified as 30 mA ±10. No MetricKind., Cumulative charge and discharge hours ('Send Times / DisCharge Times', shown in hours on the version screen). MetricKind has GeneratorRunHours and PumpRunHours but nothing equivalent for a battery.
